title: CASSE: Targeted Threat Modeling for Data Management Libraries
problem: Data management libraries (HDF5, Zarr, NetCDF) are widely used in scientific computing but their security has received minimal attention. Existing threat modeling frameworks (STRIDE) are poorly suited to DMLs' unique characteristics.
motivation: DMLs are critical infrastructure for scientific computing but security vulnerabilities could compromise entire workflows. Existing threat modeling approaches don't account for file structure complexity and domain-specific attack vectors.
method: CASSE: novel threat modeling approach for DMLs addressing STRIDE shortcomings. New attack taxonomy tailored to DML characteristics. File structure diagrams included in threat analysis. Evaluated on HDF5, NetCDF, and Zarr.
key_novelty: First threat modeling approach (CASSE) specifically designed for data management libraries, providing novel attack taxonomy and file-structure-aware analysis.
contributions: CASSE: targeted threat modeling framework for DMLs
Identified three key STRIDE shortcomings for DML analysis
Novel attack taxonomy specific to DML characteristics
File structure diagrams integrated in threat models
Application to three popular DMLs: HDF5, NetCDF, Zarr
limitations: Abstract-level presentation; detailed threat analysis not provided. Practical security solutions not addressed. Validation with DML developers/maintainers not mentioned. Applicability beyond three DMLs unclear.
primary_theme: Security threat modeling for scientific data management
